bounds.domain: Two successive request identities. Two deployments and two native port identities, including the omitted production port. One view subscriber per request and one in-flight activation callback per request; a retired callback can outlive its successor's admission.
bounds.assumptions: Synchronous request and return listeners complete. A caller uses a fresh non-aborted signal for a retry. Native event parsing is abstracted to accepted or ignored; retained events carry an opaque payload and the last accepted return replaces earlier ones.
bounds.limitations: The model covers renderer promise ownership and event routing. It excludes the view controller's native request/attempt IDs, credential slot writes and identity checks, partial host activation effects, and port registration/listener failures. Implementation cases run the broker and parser with controlled native, storage and event boundaries.

assumptions: Weak fairness of activationReply(id) for each request: every started host callback eventually fulfills or rejects. Cancellation fences publication but does not force a pending host callback to settle.
No fairness. A started host activation can remain unresolved while other renderer events continue.
